description: 450 open permits, and the AI opens with the three that need a decision. Your book cannot rank itself by consequence — it only knows clocks. TrackLynk ranks by what happens if nobody acts, so a low-risk permit expiring in ten minutes with nobody on location stays quiet.

The two failures the permit book structurally cannot show you: a permit that reads closed while the work continues, and a permit that is perfectly valid while the crew holding it has walked somewhere it does not authorize. Neither changes the permit record, so neither can be found by reading permits.

The next hour's expiries ranked by consequence rather than by clock — which permits will still have people inside them when they lapse, and which will not. The queue you should work is not the one sorted by time remaining.

Where the permit process itself leaks: a verification queue sorted by arrival rather than risk, and a night-shift extension path that requires walking back to a terminal. These are process findings, not people findings, and they are visible only when permit timestamps sit next to gate dwell and shift rosters.

Extensions, withdrawal notices and new permit records drafted from the conversation, pre-filled from the original permit and its work order. Conditions are held against physical verification — an extension cannot authorize work until the fresh gas test is actually logged.
One question spans the permit record, the work order, the location trail and the crew's shift history. Deciding whether to extend or stop stops being four system lookups and a radio call.
